senses.gloss: m. (quæstor) quæstor, military adjutant, inquisitor (v. Sm. Ant. s. v.).
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 49a:7">Sabb. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>ראהו קוס׳ אחד וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>קס׳</he>; Var. in Ar. <he>קוז׳</he>, <he>קז׳</he>) a quæstor saw him (wearing T’fillin), and he fled before him; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 795:5">Yalk. Ps. 795</cite>.

<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 8:4">Tosef. Erub. VIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 5:4">V</cite>), 4 <he>קצדור הבא לעיר וכ׳</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>קסדר</he>) when a military quæstor (commissary) takes up his station in a town for thirty days; Y. ib. VI, 23ᵇ bot. <he>הקוּסְטוֹר</he>.

<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 1049:8">Yalk. Esth. 1049</cite> <he>ולא היית כק׳ וכ׳</he> (some ed. <he>כקיס׳</he>) and thou wast not even so much as a quæstor (worthy) to run before my father’s chariot.
